title: The Line in the North
dialogue: Colonel Dusek requested the briefing at 0400. Vyktor did not argue with the hour.
monologue: Dusek does not request early briefings. She schedules them when asked. The fact that she requested means the information did not wait for morning.

narrative.text: At 2200 last night, three Tyvaren armored units crossed into the Sevagrad buffer zone — the demilitarized corridor established under the 1951 treaty. They stopped four kilometers inside the line and have not moved. They are not advancing. They are sitting.

This is not an invasion. An invasion does not stop and sit. This is a provocation — a deliberate treaty violation designed to force a response. If we respond militarily, Tyvaren escalates and blames us for the escalation. If we do not respond, the buffer zone becomes meaningless and they know it.
Tyvaren's foreign ministry has not issued any statement. The silence is intentional. They want us to move first — diplomatically or militarily. Either gives them something to work with.

dusek_standoff_brief.monologue: They stopped and sat. Dusek is right — an invasion does not stop and sit. This is a test. They are measuring whether we flinch, whether we escalate, whether we go to the Assembly and spend political capital on a military response to what they will publicly describe as a routine exercise. The correct answer is none of those. The correct answer is to make them move without giving them anything to use against us.

choices.text: File an immediate formal protest through the regional treaty commission. Demand withdrawal within 48 hours. Make the violation public before Tyvaren can frame it.
Move two Veltrian units to the border — not into the buffer zone, but visible. Match their posture without crossing the line. Force them to decide whether to escalate or withdraw.

Contact Tyvaren's foreign minister directly through back channels. No public statement. Communicate that we see the violation, we will not escalate, and we expect withdrawal within 24 hours or the treaty commission becomes unavoidable.
